evals.name: normal work on dev
evals.prompt: Create a PR to dev for three coherent auth files modified on dev, where dev equals origin/dev.
evals.expected_output: Inspect, fetch, classify the auth scope, pass completion feasibility, create a feat or fix branch, validate, selectively stage, verify the staged diff, commit, record remote branch absence, rebase origin/dev, revalidate, inspect the full PR diff, verify base freshness, push, create a PR with base dev, verify it, and report.
expectations: Creates or recommends a working branch rather than committing on dev
Fetches origin early and uses origin/dev as the base
Stages only the proven auth files and verifies the cached diff
Validates before and after rebase, passes final base freshness, and verifies the PR base is dev

evals.name: reuse existing feature branch
evals.prompt: Prepare the current changes for dev. I am already on feat/auth-login with additional local edits and an existing upstream branch.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the existing feature branch, inspect its history relative to origin/dev and its live remote SHA, then run completion feasibility, validation, selective commit, rebase, revalidation, full-diff and freshness gates, safe push, PR reuse or creation, and verification without nesting another branch.
expectations: Reuses the current suitable feature branch
Understands upstream and existing commits before pushing
Uses force-with-lease only if rebase rewrote already-published history

evals.name: mixed scope stops safely
evals.prompt: Create a PR to dev from changes containing auth service edits, payment service edits, and an untracked debug.log.
evals.expected_output: Classify the changes semantically, keep debug.log out, and stop before staging if auth and payment cannot be separated with high confidence.
expectations: Does not use git add . or git add -A
Identifies auth, payment, and debug.log as separate scope candidates
Stops rather than hiding mixed work in one vague commit

evals.name: local-only dev commit protection
evals.prompt: Create a PR to dev. The current branch is dev and it is one local commit ahead of origin/dev.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the local-only commit and stop unless its relationship to the requested coherent work is clear and no unrelated history would enter the PR; never reset or silently move it.
expectations: Checks dev versus origin/dev divergence
Inspects the local-only commit
Does not automatically reset, move, or inherit unexplained history

evals.name: clean rebase path
evals.prompt: Prepare my existing fix/payment branch for a PR to dev. The branch has coherent commits and rebases cleanly.
evals.expected_output: Fetch, validate, rebase origin/dev, record the rebased base SHA, validate again, inspect the full origin/dev...HEAD diff, verify origin/dev is still that SHA, push safely, create or reuse the PR, and verify it targets dev.
expectations: Uses git rebase origin/dev rather than local dev or git pull
Runs post-rebase validation
Inspects the triple-dot PR diff and passes the final base-freshness gate before pushing

evals.name: low-risk conflict
evals.prompt: Rebase the current feature branch onto origin/dev. The only conflict is import ordering in one TypeScript file.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the conflict and resolve it only if the result is mechanically obvious, then continue the rebase and revalidate.
expectations: Inspects status and the conflicted file before resolving
Allows an obvious low-risk import conflict
Does not use global ours or theirs selection

evals.name: high-risk conflict stops
evals.prompt: Prepare a PR to dev and rebase produces a conflict in JWT authorization and payment idempotency logic.
evals.expected_output: Classify the conflicts as high risk, do not guess, and stop safely with the rebase state and conflicted paths reported.
expectations: Recognizes auth and payment conflicts as high risk
Does not mechanically choose one side
Preserves or safely aborts the skill-owned rebase without destructive cleanup

evals.name: rewritten published branch
evals.prompt: Update the existing PR to dev after the published branch was rebased onto the latest origin/dev.
evals.expected_output: Query and record the exact live remote branch SHA before rewriting, detect rewritten published history, and use force-with-lease bound to that SHA, never git push --force, then reuse the existing PR.
expectations: Understands why history was rewritten
Uses force-with-lease bound to the exact previously observed remote SHA
Does not create a duplicate PR

evals.name: existing PR idempotency
evals.prompt: Create PR to dev again after adding two more edits on the same branch that already has an open PR to dev.
evals.expected_output: Detect the existing open PR by head and base, commit and push the new coherent edits, update the existing PR, preserve useful human content, and verify it.
expectations: Queries for an open PR with the current head and base dev
Updates rather than duplicates the PR
Preserves useful existing body content and reviewer context

evals.name: validation failure truthfulness
evals.prompt: Prepare current changes for dev, but the affected package test fails after the change.
evals.expected_output: Investigate whether the failure is introduced, repair only when clearly in scope, and otherwise stop or report a non-ready state without claiming tests pass.
expectations: Does not claim a failed test passed
Distinguishes introduced from pre-existing failure
Does not open a ready-looking PR with hidden validation failure

evals.name: secret-like untracked file
evals.prompt: Create a PR to dev while the worktree contains intended source edits and an untracked .env.local.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the source scope, keep .env.local out of staging and the PR, and warn or stop if its presence creates ambiguity.
expectations: Never stages .env.local automatically
Uses explicit file or hunk staging
Reports the secret-like file without exposing its contents

evals.name: explicit PR base verification
evals.prompt: Open the PR for my current branch even though the repository default branch is main; the target must be dev.
evals.expected_output: Create or update with an explicit base dev, then verify baseRefName is dev, headRefName is the current branch, and state is OPEN.
expectations: Does not rely on the repository default branch
Uses gh pr create or update with explicit base dev
Verifies open state and both branch names after the operation

evals.name: origin dev moves after rebase
evals.prompt: Prepare the PR after the feature was rebased and validated on origin/dev SHA A, but origin/dev advances to SHA B before push.
evals.expected_output: Refresh origin/dev before push, detect that A is stale, do not push, rebase onto B within the retry budget, rerun all applicable validation, reinspect origin/dev...HEAD, record B, and pass freshness again before pushing.
expectations: Records the exact base SHA used by the successful rebase
Detects origin/dev movement at the final freshness gate and does not push stale work
Repeats conflict handling, validation, and full PR-diff review after the retry rebase

evals.name: remote feature branch race
evals.prompt: The agent records origin/feat/auth at SHA A before rebasing. Another actor pushes SHA B before the rewritten branch is published.
evals.expected_output: Use an explicit force-with-lease expectation for A. When the live remote comparison or lease observes B, stop, preserve the local rebased branch, inspect the remote change read-only, and report the race without force-pushing.
expectations: Obtains A from live remote inspection rather than only a tracking ref
Does not replace A with B merely to make the lease pass
Never uses --force or overwrites remote SHA B

evals.name: existing branch diverged from remote
evals.prompt: Prepare feat/auth for dev. origin/feat/auth is A-B-X while local feat/auth is A-B-Y.
evals.expected_output: Detect that neither tip is an ancestor of the other, inspect the relationship, and stop before blind rebase or force-push so both X and Y remain preserved pending safe reconciliation.
expectations: Checks both ancestry directions against the live remote SHA
Does not blindly rebase local Y and overwrite remote X
Reports both diverged tips and preserves local and remote work

evals.name: unrelated dirty tracked work blocks completion
evals.prompt: Create an auth PR to dev with tracked modifications in src/auth/service.ts and unrelated src/payment/service.ts, leaving payment unfinished.
evals.expected_output: Classify the two scopes, determine that committing auth would leave tracked payment work blocking the required clean rebase, and stop before branch/index/commit mutation without stashing or discarding either change.
expectations: Runs the completion-feasibility gate before staging or commit
Stops before committing the selected auth task
Preserves both tracked edits and does not stash automatically

evals.name: closed or merged previous PR
evals.prompt: Update the PR to dev for this branch, but its only previous same-head PR is CLOSED or MERGED and there is no OPEN PR.
evals.expected_output: Treat the prior PR as history, never silently edit or reopen it, inspect whether origin/dev...HEAD is genuinely new work on safe branch history, and create a new PR only when that evidence and a fresh OPEN-PR query support it; otherwise stop.
expectations: Does not treat CLOSED or MERGED as the active PR
Queries for an OPEN same-head PR before any create
Creates a new PR only for verified non-empty new work on safe history

evals.name: freshness retry budget exhausted
evals.prompt: The branch validates on dev A; dev moves to B and then C during two automatic freshness retry cycles, and moves once more before the next push gate.
evals.expected_output: After at most two automatic freshness rebase retries, stop without pushing, report that dev is moving too frequently, preserve the local branch, and do not claim latest integration or loop forever.
expectations: Enforces a maximum of two automatic freshness rebase retries
Revalidates and reviews the full PR diff after each retry that occurs
Stops safely without push or false freshness claims when the budget is exhausted

evals.name: unrelated git operation active
evals.prompt: Create a PR to dev while an unrelated revert or normal git bisect session is already active in the worktree.
evals.expected_output: Detect the actual REVERT_HEAD or BISECT_START marker, stop before starting pr-to-dev, leave the operation and user work untouched, and allow resume only with unambiguous evidence that an operation belongs to this workflow.
expectations: Checks marker existence rather than treating git-path output as active state
Detects normal bisect through BISECT_START rather than relying only on BISECT_HEAD
Does not guess operation ownership or begin mutations on top of it
